audit_type: Post-generation comparison with held-out codebooks; manually reviewed, not blinded

issues: Generated college attendance at age 20; table codebook defines institution attended for the greatest amount of time in the four calendar years when the child turned 19-22.
Generated definition concerns highly-cited patents; the table codebook defines highly-cited inventors as the top 5% of inventors by citations within birth cohort.
results.note: Paper and codebook versions may differ; cited paper support does not settle a table-specific definition. No codebook corrections were fed back into this test generation.

coverage_gaps: Description covers only three of the 35 fields.
Inherited folder label says Table 12; supplied codebook calls this Table 10.
results.reference: Codebook-for-Table-10.pdf, annual job growth / ln_wage_growth_hs_grad / rent_twobed2015 entries
results.note: The three stated measures, periods and sources agree with the held-out codebook. This is a limited claim audit, not complete schema coverage.

issues: Claims parents are not inventors; the supplied table codebook does not impose that restriction.
Claims CZs with fewer than 1,000 children are excluded; table codebook states cells with fewer than 250 children are omitted.
Describes child-level assignments without clearly stating one row per childhood CZ.
Age 63 is placed in both income-measurement categories. Codebook and observed lag field establish a two-year lag for ages 40-63, and income at age 61 for ages 64-76.
Conflates paper-level life expectancy adjustment/extrapolation with the observed mortality table; this CSV contains ages 40-76 only.
Adds unsupported promotional wording about enhancing reliability.
results.reference: health_ineq_online_table_15_readme.pdf, page 1; age_at_d / lag in actual CSV

coverage_gaps: Only the incarceration definition is explained; parent income at percentile 25, income outcomes, and 1978-1983 cohorts are omitted.
Inherited folder label says Table 4; supplied codebook calls this Table 2.
results.note: Limited claim consistency, not a complete table description.

supported: Correct one-row-per-CZ unit; baseline incorrectly called these cities.
National income ranks and predicted adult rank at parent percentile 25 agree with the codebook.
coverage_gaps: Parent percentile 75, household income ranks and population fields are omitted.
Age-based assignment, proportional exposure and measurement-age statements require checking the referred paper sections; the table codebook alone does not establish them.

issues: Description focuses on a regression-based study method; the CSV is percentile-level outcome summaries, so it does not clearly explain the stored measurements.
supported: Grouping by parent income percentile and race/gender agrees with the table codebook.
coverage_gaps: Does not identify the 1978-1983 cohorts or explain the outcome columns.
Does not explicitly state one row per parent income percentile.

issues: Mobility-rate wording leaves the denominator ambiguous and can be read as the conditional success rate. mr_kq5_pq1 is the percent of all students with bottom-quintile parents AND top-quintile adult income; kq5_cond_parq1 is the separate conditional rate.
coverage_gaps: Only one measure is explained; access rates, median incomes, trends and college assignment are omitted.

issues: Calls exp_instr instructional expenditure per student; supplied codebook describes Total Instructional Expenditures, so the unit/denominator mapping is not established.
Calls asian_or_pacific_share_fall_2000 an Asian share, omitting Pacific Islanders.
supported: The graduation-rate period, 150%-of-normal-time measure, sticker price components and STEM-major share broadly agree with the codebook.
coverage_gaps: Emphasizes 2000 and omits the 2013 measures and college-group row definition.

pilot.adjustment_wording: Fixed: generated text refers to the paper’s adjusted estimates rather than assigning adjustment status to all CSV estimates.
remaining_errors: Default-query description introduces a false claim that life expectancy is derived from BRFSS health behaviors.
Matched-query rerun describes county, CZ and state estimates and income ventiles as table contents, although the CSV is county-level and uses quartiles.
Matched-query rerun mentions across-area standard deviation; this must not be interpreted as the sd_le fields, which are standard errors.
pilot.note: Both unsuccessful descriptions are preserved. Neither is a validated replacement for the reviewed reference description.
